title: Open homomorphisms of solvably closed Galois groups
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: An exposition of OpenAI's proof (2026) of Uchida's conjecture: for number fields F_1, F_2 and Galois extensions E_i/F_i with E_i solvably closed, every continuous homomorphism Gal(E_1/F_1) -> Gal(E_2/F_2) with open image is induced by a unique field embedding E_2 -> E_1. The first lesson introduces solvably closed fields and the maximal prosolvable extension Q^s of Q, states the conjecture and the three published results of Uchida and Hoshi that the proof uses without proof, and proves the facts on profinite Sylow subgroups, local Galois groups inside Gal(Q^s/Q) and the norm identity for active pairs. The second proves that the zero set of polynomials of degree at most d in n variables has at most d^n irreducible components, through graded prime filtrations, Hilbert polynomials and hypersurface sections. The third proves the l-adic logarithm rank theorem for m > n(n-1) points with an interpolation determinant, a zero estimate on the torus and the product formula. The fourth develops additive l-adic characters, transfer and their class-field description, proves that the Frobenius values at infinitely many primes of absolute residue degree one determine a character, and embeds a signed representation in the character space. The fifth extends the homomorphism to the normalizer of its kernel, enlarges finite quotients by regular Kummer modules, and proves that local Frobenius images generate prescribed cyclic subgroups; it follows that the extension is surjective and preserves cyclotomic logarithms for all primes l = 1 modulo [k:Q]!. The sixth describes unramified Kummer classes by S-units and proves the equivariant S-unit theorem. The seventh bounds the number of target primes missed by the local correspondence independently of l and matches residue characteristics by separating power residues. The eighth identifies the homomorphism with conjugated restriction and proves the conjecture.
prerequisites: course NT-CFT, lessons Profinite groups and infinite Galois theory (Theorem 1.2), Hilbert's Theorem 90 and Kummer theory (Theorems 3.1 and 3.3), Cyclotomic polynomials and their automorphisms, The global reciprocity law (Proposition 16.1), Ray class fields, conductors and ideal reciprocity (Proposition 18.1), Global existence and the idelic class field correspondence, The Chebotarev density theorem (Theorem 22.4)
course NT-ANT, lessons Decomposition of primes in extensions and Dirichlet's unit theorem (Theorems 9.2 and 9.4)

course NT-LOC, lessons NT-LOC-03 (Theorem 1.1, Newton lifting), NT-LOC-05 (Proposition 4.1 and the product formula, Theorem 5.2), NT-LOC-08 (Theorem 3.1, tame inertia), NT-LOC-09 (Corollary 2.2) and NT-LOC-11 (Proposition 2.1 and Theorem 3.1)
course NT-DIRL, lesson Dirichlet's theorem on primes in arithmetic progressions (Theorem 4.1)

course AG-CA, lessons The Nullstellensatz and Jacobson rings (Theorem 2.2), Associated primes and primary decomposition (Theorem 3.2), Krull dimension and Noether normalization (Proposition 1.2), Graded modules and Hilbert-Samuel functions (Theorem 3.1), Dimension theory of Noetherian local rings (Theorem 2.1)
course RT-FIN, lesson Representations and complete reducibility (Theorem 2.3, Maschke, and Corollary 4.1)
core course Abstract Algebra II (C40): Judson, Abstract Algebra: Theory and Applications, Section 15.1 (the Sylow theorems)
the named inputs (U1) Uchida's isomorphism theorem, (U2) Uchida's partial local correspondence and (H) Hoshi's criterion with Uchida's uniqueness, stated in the first lesson and used without proof

open_obligations: Named input (U1), Uchida's isomorphism theorem for solvably closed Galois extensions of number fields (Uchida 1979): used for Lemma 3.1 of the first lesson and the normalizer extension of the fifth; not proved in the programme.

Named input (U2), Uchida's partial local correspondence (Uchida 1981, Section 1 and Proposition 1; OpenAI-UC, Theorem 2.4): used for the norm identity, Frobenius generation, matching and the identification; not proved in the programme.

Named input (H), Hoshi's cyclotomic criterion (Hoshi 2025, Theorem 3.4) with Uchida's uniqueness (Uchida 1981, Proposition 2): used in the last step of the proof of the conjecture; not proved in the programme. Hoshi's proof uses Chebotarev's theorem, an exponent-two Kummer construction and Uchida's local argument; a later lesson could prove it, which would leave only Uchida's two theorems as named inputs.

Missing foundation: a course on the Neukirch-Uchida reconstruction of decomposition groups from Galois groups of solvably closed extensions would close (U1) and (U2); the programme has no such course. Saidi and Tamagawa, The m-step solvable anabelian geometry of number fields (arXiv:1909.08829), Section 1, treats the local theory and the correspondence of decomposition groups and is a free source for it.
The lessons were written and checked by one model in one session; they have not been checked by a second reader.
